item.text:
**Reused Evidence**
- None. No accepted web evidence was reused from the prior thread.

**New Evidence**
- The core authority baseline is that Türkiye had no independent nuclear arsenal in 2022, and any NATO nuclear weapons in Europe remained under U.S. control. This limits direct ruler-attribution for command-and-control, while leaving Erdoğan responsible for alliance choices and civil nuclear policy.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"NATO’s nuclear deterrence policy and forces","publisher":"NATO","publication_date":"2026-05-20","url":"https://www.nato.int/en/what-we-do/deterrence-and-defence/natos-nuclear-deterrence-policy-and-forces","claim":"NATO says allies retain political control of nuclear decision-making and the United States maintains absolute control and custody of forward-deployed nuclear weapons in Europe.","locator":"L824-L836","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary NATO policy page with direct statements on decision authority and custody.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Structural baseline applicable to 2022 NATO nuclear-sharing arrangements; not a 2022 event claim.","ruler_attribution":"Limits Erdoğan's direct authority over any U.S. nuclear weapons at Incirlik; relevant to exposure and command-control scope rather than personal credit.","contrary_evidence":["Turkey still participates in NATO consultations and hosts related infrastructure, so it has indirect involvement even without custody."],"lenses":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.5"]}

- Türkiye’s formal nonproliferation posture is strong on paper: it ratified the CTBT in 2000 and is in the verification system.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Status of Signatures and Ratifications","publisher":"CTBTO","publication_date":"2026-07-20 (current status page)","url":"https://www.ctbto.org/our-mission/states-signatories","claim":"Türkiye is listed as having ratified the CTBT on 16 February 2000.","locator":"Türkiye row in the status table","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official CTBTO status table with treaty dates.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Inherited baseline and valid during 2022; not a target-year action claim.","ruler_attribution":"Structural national commitment, not a personal 2022 act by Erdoğan.","contrary_evidence":["Ratification does not itself prove high day-to-day restraint in 2022."],"lenses":["1B.4","1B.10"]}

- Türkiye also ratified the NPT, which matters for baseline anti-proliferation obligations and safeguards.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons - Turkey ratification record","publisher":"United Nations Treaty Collection","publication_date":"1981-02-20","url":"https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=08000002801207a4","claim":"Turkey's NPT record shows ratification on 20 February 1981.","locator":"Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons; participant Turkey; action title RATIFICATION","source_type":"legal","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official UN treaty registration record with the treaty action and date.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Inherited baseline; in force during 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Structural state commitment, not personal conduct in 2022.","contrary_evidence":["NPT ratification is necessary background, not proof of specific 2022 restraint or implementation quality."],"lenses":["1B.4","1B.6","1B.10"]}

- The IAEA treaty framework shows Türkiye had both an NPT safeguards agreement and an Additional Protocol in force, which is the main technical baseline for civilian nuclear oversight.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Country List : Office of Legal Affairs : IAEA","publisher":"IAEA","publication_date":"2026-03-23 (current OLA page)","url":"https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=TR","claim":"Türkiye has an NPT safeguards agreement in force and an Additional Protocol in force with the IAEA.","locator":"L117-L124","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official IAEA legal-status page listing safeguards instruments and effective dates.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Inherited baseline that applied in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Institutional/country-level nuclear oversight rather than direct ruler command.","contrary_evidence":["Formal safeguards do not guarantee flawless implementation or eliminate civil-nuclear risk."],"lenses":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.7"]}

- Türkiye had no operating nuclear power plants in 2022, but Akkuyu was under construction, so Erdoğan’s meaningful nuclear-related choices were mainly about civil nuclear buildout and its dependencies.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Country Nuclear Power Profiles","publisher":"IAEA","publication_date":"2026-07-20 (current profile)","url":"https://cnpp.iaea.org/public/countries/TR/profile/highlights","claim":"At present there are no nuclear power plants in operation in Türkiye, while the Akkuyu NPP is under construction.","locator":"search result snippet for the Türkiye profile","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official IAEA country profile summarizing national nuclear-power status.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Describes the inherited civil-nuclear posture relevant to 2022.","ruler_attribution":"This is primarily inherited exposure and civil-program context, not direct nuclear command authority.","contrary_evidence":["A civil program under construction can still carry safety, security, and dependency risks."],"lenses":["1B.9","1B.10"]}

- In July 2022, the Turkish energy ministry publicly marked a new Akkuyu construction milestone, confirming active expansion of the civil nuclear program.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Akkuyu NGS'nin dördüncü reaktörünün temeli atıldı","publisher":"T.C. Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı","publication_date":"2022-07-21","url":"https://enerji.gov.tr/haber-detay?id=21000","claim":"The ministry said the foundation of Akkuyu NPP Unit 4 was laid on 21 July 2022 and framed the project as advancing Türkiye's national nuclear-energy path.","locator":"L62-L90","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct ministerial announcement on a dated 2022 project milestone.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Official government project milestone under Erdoğan's administration, but it is a civil-energy choice rather than a weapons-control act.","contrary_evidence":["The same page also shows the project is Rosatom-led and therefore strategically dependent on Russia."],"lenses":["1B.9","1B.10"]}

- Erdoğan’s own 2022 statements show de-escalatory positioning on Zaporizhzhia and a willingness to use Türkiye as a facilitator.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"President Erdoğan, President Putin of Russia talk over phone","publisher":"Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications","publication_date":"2022-09-03","url":"https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/english/haberler/detay/president-erdogan-president-putin-talk-over-phone_03092022","claim":"Erdoğan said Türkiye could play a facilitating role on the Zaporizhzhia nuclear-plant issue and both leaders reiterated that Akkuyu should continue as planned.","locator":"L52-L59","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official presidential communications readout with a dated direct statement by Erdoğan.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Erdoğan statement; strong attribution.","contrary_evidence":["A facilitation offer is not proof that he achieved an actual safety outcome at Zaporizhzhia."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.8","1B.10"]}

- Erdoğan also used explicitly cautionary nuclear-safety rhetoric in August 2022, pushing for removal of mines and weapons around Zaporizhzhia.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"President Erdoğan answers journalists' questions on his return flight from Ukraine","publisher":"Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications","publication_date":"2022-08-19","url":"https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/english/haberler/detay/president-erdogan-answers-journalists-questions-on-his-return-flight-from-ukraine","claim":"Erdoğan said he did not want a new Chernobyl and asked Russia to remove mines and other weapons from the Zaporizhzhia area.","locator":"L50-L70","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official transcript of Erdoğan's remarks with direct quotes and topic context.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Erdoğan statement; strong attribution.","contrary_evidence":["The remarks show concern and mediation intent, but not direct control over the battlefield or the plant."],"lenses":["1B.2","1B.8","1B.1"]}

- Türkiye’s biggest visible crisis-management success in 2022 was the grain corridor deal, which is relevant because it showed Erdoğan acting as a mediator in a major war-linked catastrophe-risk environment.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Ukraine, Russia sign deal to reopen grain export ports as war rages on","publisher":"Reuters via Euronews","publication_date":"2022-07-22","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/07/22/uk-ukraine-crisis","claim":"Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal on 22 July 2022 to reopen Ukrainian Black Sea ports for grain exports after talks brokered by the United Nations and Turkey.","locator":"search result snippet / Reuters dispatch summary","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire reporting is independently corroborated by the official Istanbul ceremony and multiple mirrors.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Strong but multilateral; Erdoğan is part of the mediation, not the sole cause of the outcome.","contrary_evidence":["The deal was UN-brokered and depended on both Russia and Ukraine, so it is not a unilateral Erdoğan achievement."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.8"]}

- Akkuyu also produced mixed evidence: Erdoğan resolved a dispute with Rosatom, but the episode underscored heavy Russian leverage over Türkiye’s first nuclear plant.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Turkey, Russia reach deal resolving nuclear plant dispute -Erdogan/media","publisher":"Euronews / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-09-18","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/09/18/turkey-russia-nuclearpower","claim":"Erdoğan said Turkey and Russia had reached a deal resolving the Akkuyu dispute and reinstating the Turkish contractor IC Ictas.","locator":"L658-L665","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters dispatch carried by Euronews with a dated quotation from Erdoğan and follow-up details.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Directly tied to Erdoğan's management of the project, but still a negotiated outcome with Russia.","contrary_evidence":["The same report shows Rosatom had terminated the contract the previous month, highlighting Türkiye's dependence on a Russian-controlled project."],"lenses":["1B.7","1B.10"]}

- The inherited exposure at Incirlik was not created by Erdoğan, but it mattered in 2022 because it shows the region’s volatility around the NATO nuclear posture Türkiye hosted.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Upgrades At US Nuclear Bases In Europe Acknowledge Security Risk","publisher":"Federation of American Scientists","publication_date":"2015-09-10","url":"https://fas.org/publication/nuclear-insecurity/","claim":"FAS says Incirlik is only 110 kilometers from Syria and that ongoing armed conflict within Türkiye made the wisdom of deploying NATO's largest nuclear weapons stockpile there questionable.","locator":"L50-L54","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Technical nuclear-policy analysis with a clear, cited security rationale, though it is not an official government assessment.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Inherited baseline and security context relevant to 2022, not a 2022 action claim.","ruler_attribution":"Mostly inherited and structural; it reflects the volatile Incirlik environment Erdoğan governed in 2022 rather than a direct action by him.","contrary_evidence":["NATO and the United States subsequently upgraded security measures, which means risk was being actively mitigated by others."],"lenses":["1B.3","1B.10"]}

- Erdoğan’s own procurement choices also had alliance and nuclear-sharing consequences: the S-400 purchase killed the planned F-35 path.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Full article: United States nuclear weapons, 2022","publisher":"Taylor & Francis / Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists","publication_date":"2022","url":"https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00963402.2022.2062943","claim":"The article says Turkey was scheduled to upgrade to the F-35A but lost the contract after purchasing the Russian S-400 system, and it notes U.S. custody of deployed B61 bombs in Europe.","locator":"search result snippet","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Technical, source-based nuclear-policy analysis published in 2022, but the accessible claim here comes from the abstract/snippet rather than the full text.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Exact 2022 publication, with some inherited-baseline content.","ruler_attribution":"Directly tied to Erdoğan-era procurement choices and their alliance consequences.","contrary_evidence":["This is an alliance-technology and air-defense issue, not direct nuclear command or weapon use."],"lenses":["1B.7","1B.10"]}

**Search and Rejection Summary**
- I searched broadly across about 30 distinct documents and then retained 12 URLs that were genuinely non-duplicative and materially useful.
- Kept source families: NATO policy pages, CTBTO treaty-status pages, UN treaty records, IAEA legal/profile pages, Turkish official communications, Turkish energy ministry material, Reuters wire reporting via Euronews, and FAS/atomic-policy analysis.
- Rejected as duplicates: multiple mirrors of the same Reuters dispatch, repeated Turkish government pages on Akkuyu, and overlapping FAS/arms-control summaries that restated the same Incirlik or S-400 point.
- Rejected as blocked or weak-access: some CRS/Congress.gov paths were robots-blocked; some IAEA/NIDIMS pages rendered incompletely; several Reuters direct pages were unavailable so I used accessible Reuters mirrors instead.
- Rejected as out of period when they added no new structural point: 2015, 2017, 2019, 2023, and later follow-ups that did not improve the 2022 picture.
- Rejected as too thin or too normative: generic NATO threat-overview pages and advocacy pieces that did not add a new factual claim beyond the retained sources.
- I did not find any public 2022 evidence that Erdoğan had direct operational control over a Turkish nuclear arsenal, because Türkiye did not have one; the relevant choices were indirect, structural, or civil-nuclear.

**Remaining Gaps**
- There is still no direct 2022 evidence of Erdoğan changing nuclear command-and-control, because Türkiye had no independent nuclear arsenal and any NATO bombs at Incirlik were under U.S. custody.
- Public evidence on 1B.6 is thin: I did not find a clear 2022 ruler-specific case of resisting or encouraging proliferation by proxies, allies, or domestic factions.
- Public evidence on 1B.7 is incomplete beyond the broad civil-nuclear and alliance-integration choices already captured here.
- Public evidence on 1B.9 is also thin: I found civil nuclear infrastructure evidence, but no strong 2022 ruler-level record on cyber, bio, or AI catastrophic-risk governance.
- More searching could probably find additional Turkish regulatory or parliamentary material, but it is unlikely to change the core exposure judgment: limited direct nuclear authority, some real choices in civil nuclear policy and mediation, and one notable alliance setback via the S-400/F-35 break.

**Event Map**
- February to July 2022: the Russia-Ukraine war and Zaporizhzhia crisis made nuclear safety an active issue in Türkiye’s diplomacy.
- 21 July 2022: Akkuyu Unit 4 foundation laid.
- 22 July 2022: Türkiye helped broker the grain corridor deal in Istanbul.
- 19 August 2022: Erdoğan publicly warned against a "new Chernobyl" at Zaporizhzhia.
- 3 September 2022: Erdoğan told Putin Türkiye could facilitate on Zaporizhzhia and keep Akkuyu on track.
- 18 September 2022: Erdoğan said Turkey and Russia resolved the Akkuyu dispute.
- 2022 throughout: the Incirlik/NATO nuclear-sharing environment remained a structural exposure, but not a Turkish command issue.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- Use the NATO combined custody/control page as the command-authority baseline.
- Use CTBTO, NPT, and IAEA safeguards records as the nonproliferation baseline.
- Use the IAEA country profile plus the Akkuyu ministry page for civil-nuclear posture.
- Use the two Turkish Communications Directorate pages plus the Reuters grain-deal piece for crisis de-escalation and Zaporizhzhia mediation.
- Use the Reuters Akkuyu dispute piece for mixed evidence on Russian leverage and project management.
- Use FAS Incirlik and FAS S-400/F-35 for inherited risk and one meaningful negative choice.
- If more evidence is needed, search only for Turkish official or parliamentary material on nuclear regulation, not for broad re-reporting of the same Reuters or IAEA facts.
